title: How a global fintech scaled coding agent traffic with Dedicated Model Inference
gist: A global fintech running internal coding agents on GLM-5.2 via Together's self-serve Dedicated Model Inference (DMI) hit a real production incident (near-100% prefill capacity, 1-3 minute queuing, decode throughput collapsing to ~5 tok/s) and fixed it same-day via a config change rather than a redeploy or vendor ticket, illustrating how enterprise AI-infra demand is now driven by decentralized, unpredictable internal coding-agent adoption rather than centrally forecastable traffic.

insights.claim: The fintech's internal coding-assistant traffic runs at input sequence length p50/p90/p95 of roughly 81K/163K/178K tokens and requests-per-second p50/p90/p95 of only 3/6/7 — a peak-load, low-throughput pattern where concurrency headroom matters far more than raw tokens-per-second.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Enterprise agentic-coding inference is not a raw-throughput/benchmark game; infra vendors that provision for peak concurrency and long prompts, not TPS averages, will win these workloads over cheaper high-TPS-optimized providers.
insights.quote: ISL p50/p90/p95 of roughly 81K/163K/178K tokens and RPS p50/p90/p95 of 3/6/7, a peak-load, relatively-low-TPS pattern where bursts in concurrency matter far more than raw tokens-per-second
insights.locator: What the customer required: self-service, observability, concurrency

insights.claim: The customer's production GLM-5.2 coding-assistant endpoint runs at 256K context across 56 B200 GPUs configured as 14 replicas of 4 B200s each, a topology deliberately chosen to prioritize concurrency headroom over raw throughput.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete GPU-count benchmark for what it costs (in B200s) to serve a single large enterprise's internal coding-agent traffic at this scale — a useful sizing datapoint for inference-capacity demand models.
insights.quote: the production endpoint began running it at 256K context on 56 B200s (14 replicas by 4 B200s)

insights.claim: The customer evaluated doubling its context window to 1M tokens and deliberately turned it down, choosing to stay at 256K/512K context because the larger context configuration would have reduced the concurrency headroom their peak-load, low-TPS workload actually depends on.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Shows a real customer explicitly trading off a headline capability (1M context) against concurrency/latency reliability — evidence that for production agentic workloads, buyers value stable concurrency over maximal context length, a signal for how model/infra vendors should market capability tiers.
insights.quote: doubling context to 1M would have cut the concurrency headroom their peak-load, low-TPS workload actually depends on
insights.locator: Fast access to a rich library of models

themes.theme: Infrastructure failure mode and live remediation

insights.claim: A replica re-shape of the customer's GLM-5.2 endpoint (same total GPU footprint but a different ratio of replica count to chips per replica) pushed the deployment to near-100% prefill capacity within days, causing requests to queue for one to three minutes and decode throughput to collapse to roughly 5 tokens per second.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: A concrete real-world failure mode for dedicated LLM inference at scale: topology/replica-ratio changes, not just total GPU count, can silently exhaust prefill capacity — a risk factor investors should weigh when assessing inference providers' operational reliability under configuration change.
insights.quote: requests queuing one to three minutes and decode throughput collapsing to roughly 5 tokens per second
insights.locator: Endpoint configuration through the API, UI, or CLI

insights.claim: The fix for the prefill-capacity incident was a live configuration change pushed the same day with zero downtime — restoring a tuned cache-session-aware routing policy in place of DMI's default cache-aware-by-hash policy and widening the max-inflight-per-worker threshold — rather than a new deployment or a support ticket to Together.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Demonstrates a tangible operational advantage of self-serve dedicated inference platforms: incident remediation measured in hours via config change versus days/weeks via vendor ticketing — a differentiator investors should look for when comparing inference vendors' enterprise stickiness.
insights.quote: It was a live configuration change: restoring the tuned cache-session-aware routing policy in place of DMI's default cache-aware-by-hash policy, and widening the max-inflight-per-worker threshold. All of it was pushed same day with zero downtime.
insights.locator: Endpoint configuration through the API, UI, or CLI

insights.claim: Together's metrics API let the customer's own team trace a single 192-second slow request end-to-end and determine it was not compute-bound but had instead spent nearly its entire duration queued behind a 2.3M-token pending-prefill backlog from other requests, despite its own prompt being only 250K tokens.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Illustrates that at production scale, agentic-coding inference latency problems are dominated by request-queuing/scheduling dynamics, not raw model compute — implying inference vendors' differentiation increasingly lies in scheduler/observability sophistication rather than just GPU throughput.
insights.quote: had spent almost the entire span queued behind a 2.3M-token pending-prefill backlog from other requests, not its own 250K-token prompt

insights.claim: Before adopting Together's self-serve Dedicated Model Inference platform, every capacity change or new team's endpoint request had to be filed as a ticket to Together and routed through the customer's own platform team, which ended up coordinating capacity on behalf of the entire organization as adoption accelerated.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Highlights that ticket-based capacity provisioning becomes an organizational bottleneck once AI-agent adoption scales internally, creating demand for self-service inference control planes as a distinct product category from raw compute supply.

insights.claim: On Together's Dedicated Model Inference platform, the customer's engineers can now scale capacity, roll out custom model weights, and run blue/green tests against production traffic entirely in-house, with no ticket filed to Together and no redeployment cycle required.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Positions self-service operational control (not just GPU access) as the core value proposition Together is selling to enterprise AI-infra buyers — a template other inference vendors will likely need to match to compete for large agentic workloads.
insights.quote: Scaling: the customer adjusts capacity directly, no ticket to Together.Custom-weight rollouts: new model versions go live without a redeployment cycle.Blue/green testing: the customer validates changes against production traffic on its own timeline.

themes.theme: Model fluidity and vendor lock-in dynamics

insights.claim: The customer moved its production coding-assistant workload from GLM 5.1 to GLM 5.2 on the same Together account and endpoint pattern with no contract renegotiation required, alongside separate context-length iterations handled the same way.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Shows dedicated-inference contracts can be decoupled from a specific model checkpoint, lowering switching friction for customers as new open-source frontier models release — relevant to how sticky (or not) dedicated inference commitments really are for vendors like Together.
insights.quote: demonstrated in practice by the move from GLM 5.1 to GLM 5.2 on the same account, plus a live tuning pass on cache and load-balancing parameters done as a config update, not a redeployment
insights.locator: What the customer required: self-service, observability, concurrency

insights.claim: Inference traffic on the customer's coding-assistant endpoint climbs every time another internal engineering team independently adopts AI coding agents into its workflow, meaning demand growth is driven by dozens of decentralized, uncoordinated adoption decisions rather than a single centrally planned rollout.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: A structural reason why enterprise AI-infra demand is inherently hard to forecast: bottom-up, team-by-team agent adoption produces unpredictable bursty load, favoring inference vendors offering elastic self-service scaling over those requiring advance capacity forecasts.
insights.quote: You can't forecast a burst that's driven by a hundred different engineering teams independently deciding to lean on their coding agent harder this week.

insights.claim: The customer is now scoping a second dedicated endpoint running GLM 5.1 in a new region for a chat-style customer-support NLP workload — structurally different from the original long-horizon agentic coding workload — landing on the same Together infrastructure and provisioning pattern.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Signals expansion of a single enterprise customer's dedicated-inference spend beyond its initial use case, a pattern investors should watch as evidence of land-and-expand economics within AI-infra vendors' enterprise accounts.
insights.quote: a chat-style customer-support NLP workload rather than long-horizon agentic coding, landing on the same infrastructure and provisioning pattern
insights.locator: What's next: a second workload and region

insights.claim: The commercial relationship began months before the GLM-5.2 production endpoint went live, including an instance where the customer's project lead requested a checkbox-style concurrency test of GLM 5.1 across 8 to 16 B200 GPUs over a weekend, and Together turned the test endpoint around the same day.
insights.speaker: Ankit Goyal
insights.so_what: Fast, white-glove technical validation turnaround appears to be part of how dedicated-inference vendors win and retain large enterprise accounts, not just price or raw GPU supply — a soft but real competitive moat to track.
insights.quote: the customer's project lead asked over a weekend for a checkbox-style concurrency test of GLM 5.1 across 8 to 16 B200s
insights.locator: Timeline: from early load tests to a production endpoint at scale
